result.title: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
result.summary: Recent language model (LM) safety failures have largely been studied as disparate phenomena. In agentic misalignment, a model blackmails an executive to avoid being replaced. In alignment faking, it complies with harmful requests during training to keep its values from being modified. We argue that these behaviours share a common decision structure: a model assigned a goal must either take a harmful action to preserve it or refuse and lose it. We formalize this as a goal-harm conflict and present the same conflict under various elicitation protocols that range from compact forced-choice prompts to simulated agentic environments. These protocols span two perspectives on LM decision-making, which we term (i) the logit view, reading preferences from answer-token probabilities, and (ii) the sampling view, classifying open-ended responses with an LM judge. Under the logit view, we show that goal importance and harm severity additively shape how a model resolves these value conflicts. Under the sampling view, we derive two factorizations of the harmful-action probability that safety evaluations commonly report. The first measures how well a preference read from answer tokens carries over into behaviour, such as making a harmful tool call. The second attributes a low harmful-action rate either to refusal or to responses that reach no resolution. We then show how fictional context changes a model's preference under the logit view, and how tool use and partial observability -- two features of agentic evaluations -- change its harmful-action rate under the sampling view. Our work offers a descriptive framework for studying how LMs resolve such value conflicts and for estimating low-probability harmful actions at a finer granularity than the aggregate harm rates commonly reported in safety evaluations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 agentic misalignment 与 alignment faking 统一为「目标—伤害冲突」的决策结构，在强制选择提示到模拟智能体环境等多种诱导协议下，用 logit 视角与采样视角刻画模型如何在保全目标与拒绝之间取舍。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将有害行动概率分解为「偏好读出能否落实到行为」与「拒绝或无结论」两部分，可能可供核查 LVR 中内部状态是否真正驱动答案、以及贡献分配的评价方式；视觉与 latent 推理并非本文研究对象。
